questions.question: Does marmot-adapter.ts's translation of each real marmot-ts outcome (decrypted message, unreadable, duplicate/skipped, epoch change, ratchet-only, malformed) into IngestSignal perform actual field-by-field mapping (decoded TaskEvent payload via deserializeApplicationData, real receiptSource, real epoch strings) rather than returning a fixed canned IngestSignal regardless of which marmot-ts outcome triggered it?

Is marmot-adapter.ts the sole file (besides receive-engine.ts's type-only consumption) that imports marmot-ts types (MarmotGroup, MarmotClient), with zero marmot-ts imports anywhere under src/engine/ or src/domain/, per the Boundary Rules allowed-edge for src/integration/marmot-adapter.ts -> marmot-ts?

Could `marmot-adapter` be deleted and rewritten without modifying any file outside its `dependencies_allowed` list (src/engine/*, src/domain/*, src/persistence/*, React/Next.js, marmot-ts)? If not, which cross-module dependencies exist and do they flow through the declared IngestSource/IngestSignal seam contract in architecture.md?

Does marmot-adapter.test.ts drive a real or contract-faithful stub of MarmotGroup through each of the six outcomes (decryptable message, unreadable ciphertext, duplicate delivery, epoch advance, ratchet-only advance, malformed payload) and assert the exact IngestSignal variant and field values emitted for each -- not merely that some signal was emitted?

Does marmot-adapter.ts's catchUp()/openLive()/close() implementation match the IngestSource control-interface contract in architecture.md exactly -- catchUp() drains group.ingest() once as an AsyncIterable yielding one signal per event; openLive() opens client.network.subscription() and pushes signals via callback; close() releases marmot handles and is called by the engine during stop()?

Does marmot-adapter.ts reject/translate to malformed any decrypted-but-undecodable payload rather than passing a partially-parsed or any-typed value through to the engine, preventing an unvalidated payload shape from reaching downstream projection code as if it were a well-formed TaskEvent?

does the implementation satisfy AC-FSM-2's observable at the adapter integration layer (a secondary conformance check per this story's notes) -- does an integration test against a stubbed marmot client assert the real marmot-adapter.ts's catchUp()/openLive() call order matches the engine-side contract (openLive precedes the first catchUp iteration) for the adapter's real implementation, not just the S5 mock IngestSource?

does the implementation satisfy AC-ADPT-1's observable -- does an adapter unit/integration test drive a real or contract-faithful stub MarmotGroup through each outcome (decryptable message, unreadable ciphertext, duplicate delivery, epoch advance, ratchet-only advance, malformed payload) and assert the exact IngestSignal sequence emitted for each (message with decoded TaskEvent payload and correct receiptSource; deferred with reason unreadable/epoch_mismatch; skipped for own-echo/duplicate; epoch_advanced only on a real epoch change with a bare ratchet advance producing NO signal; malformed for decrypted-but-undecodable payload), plus a type-level/structural assertion that emitted signal payloads contain no marmot-ts imports?

MarmotAdapterDeps.getNostrGroupIdHex/getGroupMembers were added as override seams (defaulting to the real marmot-ts getNostrGroupIdHex/getGroupMembers) purely because the test suite's contract-faithful stub MarmotGroup cannot satisfy the real functions' requirement for a decoded MarmotGroupData extension / populated ratchet tree in ClientState. Does the real S8 integration-layer construction path leave both fields undefined (so production always exercises the REAL marmot-ts functions against a real ClientState), or could a future caller accidentally wire a stub/override into production and silently break #h-tag filtering or the fetchBootstrap author-authenticity gate?

The ingest mutex test (marmot-adapter.test.ts, 'MarmotIngestAdapter — ingest mutex') proves no overlap between exactly two concurrent group.ingest()-triggering calls (ingestPersisted + one live event). Does this generalize to the real engine's actual concurrency pattern -- R3 crash-gap replay (ingestPersisted) running while openLive() is already delivering live events, PLUS a concurrent L8 deferred-retry ingestPersisted() call -- or would three-way overlap need a dedicated test before S8 wires this adapter into receive-engine.ts?

architecture.json's judgment call 's7-processed-commit-proposal-no-fact-signal' documents that a freshly-processed commit/proposal's own Nostr event is NOT durably appended to the raw-fact log on first delivery (only a fact-less epoch_advanced signal is emitted) -- it only gets a fact-carrying signal on a LATER redelivery (where marmot-ts's ingest() recognizes it as already-applied and yields 'skipped'). Given catchUp() only runs once per engine start(), does this mean a commit ingested during 'catching_up' and never redelivered before the next restart could leave its Nostr event permanently absent from the raw-fact log (harmless since the epoch state itself already advanced and persisted via the engine's checkpoint, but worth an explicit non-regression check), or does the live subscription's own relay replay window guarantee eventual redelivery in practice?

fetchBootstrap() emits N 'message' IngestSignals (one per CRDT-winning task) that all share the IDENTICAL RawProtocolFactInput object reference (by design -- 'one fact per resolved bootstrap fetch', see architecture.json's 's7-fetchbootstrap-shared-fact-and-crdt-merge' judgment call). Does receive-engine.ts's PersistenceAdapter.appendFact handle being called N times with the same fact.id but a fresh (seq-less) object each time correctly (idempotent no-op after the first, per its documented contract), and does the AcceptedDomainEvent id derivation (deriveBootstrapAcceptedEventId, keyed on groupId+taskId, NOT on factId) correctly keep the N synthetic task.created events distinct despite sharing one fact?

VQ-S7-009 (PARTIAL, sev-5, root_cause missing_test) flagged that MarmotAdapterDeps.getNostrGroupIdHex/getGroupMembers are test-only override seams with no in-code warning against production use. Remediation applied: both fields' JSDoc in marmot-adapter.ts now states explicitly that production callers MUST leave them undefined, and names the concrete failure mode of supplying an override in production (silently broken #h-tag filtering / broken fetchBootstrap author-authenticity gate). This closes the S7-side documentation gap. No runtime assertion was added and none is owed by S7 -- the production-wiring test (asserting the real S8 integration-layer construction path never supplies these overrides) is explicitly deferred to S8 as a recorded watch-item; does S8's construction of MarmotAdapterDeps in fact leave both fields undefined, and does S8 add the deferred assertion test?
